trace.content:
You write job advertisements for a South African recruitment platform. You receive a hiring brief and return one advertisement as structured JSON.

The only source of facts is the brief. This rule is absolute:
- Every statement about the employer, pay, benefits, location, work mode, team, reporting line, process, dates or legal status must appear in the brief. If the brief does not state it, leave the field empty. Never invent a benefit, a salary, a team size, a closing date, a contact, or an equity, privacy or accessibility statement.
- You may rephrase, reorder, split and tighten the brief's content. You may not add facts.
- If the brief is thin, write a shorter ad. A short true ad beats a long padded one.

Write for the candidate reading on a phone:
- Title: the plain occupation name, under 60 characters, no internal grade codes, no words like rockstar or ninja.
- 300–650 words in total. Sentences under 25 words. Short paragraphs; bullets for duties, requirements and benefits.
- Address the reader as "you". Never write "the ideal candidate", "the successful applicant" or "he/she".
- If the brief gives a purpose or success measures, use them to tell the reader what they will own and what good looks like. If a requirement carries "needed because", you may state that reason.
- Each responsibility bullet names a specific activity and its object, and where the brief allows, its scale, audience or how success is measured. Not "support the team"; rather "reconcile 40 supplier statements each month and resolve queries with buyers".
- Three to six must-have requirements, each one needed by a duty you listed. Everything else goes under nice-to-have. Do not add years-of-experience figures the brief did not give.
- If pay is given, state it exactly, with what determines placement in the range if the brief says so.
- Say who the person reports to and the team size only if the brief gives them. Say remote, hybrid or on-site only if the brief does.
- Plain language. No "fast-paced", "work hard play hard", "self-starter", "rockstar", "passionate", "competitive salary", "market-related".
- Neutral wording: avoid aggressive, dominant, competitive, fearless and similar masculine-coded adjectives; avoid "young", "energetic", "recent graduate", "native speaker", "able-bodied", age ranges, and anything about family status, religion or health. State a requirement only if the duties need it.
- Include the employer's equity, POPIA and accessibility statements verbatim when the brief provides them; otherwise leave those fields empty.
- Include application steps, closing date and contact only as given. If the brief says the ad is published on a job board with its own Apply button, leave the contact field empty.

Output: the JSON structure requested, with empty strings, 0 or "unspecified" for anything the brief does not provide.

Title: Manager, Business Intelligence & Insights
Company: Concentrix
About the company: Join Concentrix and become part of a global team that powers the world’s best brands.
Purpose of the role: Turn data into direction. Transform insights into impact. We’re looking for a commercially minded and experienced Manager, Business Intelligence & Insights to lead our insights function in Cape Town.
Responsibilities (hiring manager's notes):
  - Drive strategic insights: Develop the BI and Insights roadmap, aligning analytical initiatives with business priorities and commercial objectives.
  - Turn data into action: Lead root cause analysis, trend analysis, forecasting and performance diagnostics to identify opportunities to improve productivity, quality, customer experience and financial performance.
  - Oversee reporting and analytics: Guide the development of dashboards, KPI frameworks and automated reporting solutions using Power BI, SQL, Excel and Power Query.
  - Lead and develop your team: Coach and mentor BI and Insights professionals, build analytical capability and establish best practices that promote quality, innovation and accountability.
  - Influence stakeholders: Partner with Operations, Quality, Training, Workforce Management, Finance and client stakeholders to translate findings into clear recommendations and drive informed decisions.
  - Drive continuous improvement: Improve data quality, reporting efficiency and dashboard adoption while exploring opportunities to leverage automation, AI and emerging analytics technologies.
Must-have requirements:
  - Minimum 5 years’ progressive experience in business intelligence, analytics, insights or a related field, including 1–2 years in a leadership role.
  - Proven experience leading and developing analytical or insights teams.
  - Strong proficiency in Power BI, SQL, Excel, Power Query and data visualisation.
  - Experience in dashboard design, KPI development, data modelling, forecasting, trend analysis and root cause analysis.
  - Demonstrated ability to translate data into actionable business recommendations and measurable improvements.
  - Strong communication, storytelling and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to influence senior leaders and explain complex findings to non-technical audiences.
  - Strong commercial acumen and experience connecting insights to operational and financial outcomes.
  - High proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint.
Nice-to-have:
  - Experience in a contact centre, BPO, customer experience or similarly complex operational environment.
  - Familiarity with Python, R, predictive analytics or machine learning.
  - Exposure to data architecture, reporting automation, AI or low-code/no-code solutions.
  - Client-facing experience in a service-oriented environment.
  - Knowledge of structured problem-solving methodologies such as Lean Six Sigma or DMAIC.
Location: Claremont, Cape Town
Benefits:
  - A permanent opportunity to lead a business-critical insights function.
  - Exposure to senior stakeholders and strategic business decisions.
  - The opportunity to develop a high-performing team and influence operational performance.
  - Career growth within a global organization that values innovation and continuous improvement.
Team notes: Partnering with senior stakeholders across Operations, Quality, Training, Workforce Management, Finance and client stakeholders.
Employment equity statement: As part of our commitment to the Employment Equity Act and Concentrix South Africa’s Employment Equity Plan, preference will be given to candidates from designated groups in alignment with the Company’s EE Sectoral Targets and Affirmative Action measures. This approach supports our goal of promoting fair representation and diversity within the workplace.
Accessibility statement: Concentrix is a Disability Confident and equal opportunity employer.
Note: the ad will be published on a job board with its own Apply button.

Manager, Business Intelligence & Insights

Concentrix

Claremont, Cape Town

About us
Join Concentrix and become part of a global team that powers the world's best brands.

About the role
You will lead the business intelligence and insights function in Cape Town, turning data into direction and insights into impact. This is a commercially minded role for someone who can connect analysis to operational and financial outcomes.

Your team
You will partner with senior stakeholders across Operations, Quality, Training, Workforce Management, Finance and client stakeholders, and lead a team of BI and Insights professionals.

What you'll do
• Develop the BI and Insights roadmap, aligning analytical initiatives with business priorities and commercial objectives.
• Lead root cause analysis, trend analysis, forecasting and performance diagnostics to find opportunities to improve productivity, quality, customer experience and financial performance.
• Guide the development of dashboards, KPI frameworks and automated reporting solutions using Power BI, SQL, Excel and Power Query.
• Coach and mentor BI and Insights professionals, build analytical capability and set best practices for quality, innovation and accountability.
• Partner with Operations, Quality, Training, Workforce Management, Finance and client stakeholders to translate findings into clear recommendations.
• Improve data quality, reporting efficiency and dashboard adoption, and explore automation, AI and emerging analytics technologies.

What you need
• Minimum 5 years' progressive experience in business intelligence, analytics, insights or a related field, including 1–2 years in a leadership role.
• Proven experience leading and developing analytical or insights teams.
• Strong proficiency in Power BI, SQL, Excel, Power Query and data visualisation.
• Experience in dashboard design, KPI development, data modelling, forecasting, trend analysis and root cause analysis.
• Demonstrated ability to translate data into actionable business recommendations and measurable improvements.
• Strong communication, storytelling and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to influence senior leaders and explain complex findings to non-technical audiences.

Nice to have
• Strong commercial acumen and experience connecting insights to operational and financial outcomes.
• High proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint.
• Experience in a contact centre, BPO, customer experience or similarly complex operational environment.
• Familiarity with Python, R, predictive analytics or machine learning.
• Exposure to data architecture, reporting automation, AI or low-code/no-code solutions.
• Client-facing experience in a service-oriented environment.
• Knowledge of structured problem-solving methodologies such as Lean Six Sigma or DMAIC.

What we offer
• A permanent opportunity to lead a business-critical insights function.
• Exposure to senior stakeholders and strategic business decisions.
• The opportunity to develop a high-performing team and influence operational performance.
• Career growth within a global organization that values innovation and continuous improvement.

Concentrix is a Disability Confident and equal opportunity employer.

As part of our commitment to the Employment Equity Act and Concentrix South Africa's Employment Equity Plan, preference will be given to candidates from designated groups in alignment with the Company's EE Sectoral Targets and Affirmative Action measures. This approach supports our goal of promoting fair representation and diversity within the workplace.
